recipes.name: German Hamburgers (Frikadellen)
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Soak kaiser roll in a medium bowl of water for 10 minutes. Drain and squeeze out excess water; crumble roll into a large bowl.
Add ground meats, onion, parsley, egg, paprika, salt, and black pepper to crumbled roll; mix until well blended. Shape mixture into 8 equal-sized patties.

Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Fry patties in the hot skillet until browned and no longer pink in the center, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a patty should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: German Hamburgers (Frikadellen)
raw_recipe.description: This frikadellen recipe with ground pork and beef, onion, parsley, egg, and hot paprika makes a batch of delicious pan-fried German meat patties.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make the original hamburger, pan-fried and served like a flattened meatball. Make it a meal, and serve the burgers with steamed string beans and a fresh tossed salad. You can also serve them on a Kaiser roll with lettuce, tomato, pickled cucumbers, finely sliced deep fried onions and curry ketchup. Remember to keep your finished burgers warm in the oven as you continue to cook the rest in a skillet.

review.reviewBody: This is a meal that is celebrated in many countries! Especially Europe and the Scandinavian countries. Part of the appeal is those seared edges and the softer centers. Putting the whole blob in a loaf pan and cooking as a loaf with NONE of the seared edges is not the recipe. If you want a meatloaf, make a meatloaf. If you want Frikadellen, follow the directions. But do not slam someone's recipe because you screwed it up and didn't like the mess you made. I do not think folks who totally change a recipe should have their rating counted. Just saying.

As a Chef, and as our friend Chef Jean Pierre has always correctly emphasized saying; "Onyo is always number first!" And I could never disagree for the life of me! When in a meat patty such as this 'German Hamburger' and as my Mom used to make, always ALWAYS sauté the 'onyo' slowly until it's 'caramelized' .... and lacking to do so, you will never be able to extract the natural sweetness from the onion! Just sauté the onion FIRST real slow and low, let cool and then incorporate the sweetness into this recipe that is also missing out on freshly grated Garlic and Marjoram.Once done, and MOST importantly that you sear the patties so they attain 'crisy' edges, lacking to do so will leave you with a soft soggy meat-loafy texture which is NOT a German hamburger! Also, it is never served on a bun but instead with a classic Mushroom Sauce, 'Pilzsoße' .... and only then, this will be the real 'Frikadellen' .... Enjoy!

I often make these but make them the way my German mother did. It is basically the same recipe but we don't add parsley. And the other thing I do is coat each Frikadell in either cornflake crumbs or bread crumbs. I fry them up in butter and oil and add milk towards the end to create a super yummy gravy! Sheesh....now I'm hungry!!!!

I don't need a recipe, but just wanted to comment as one look at the picture made me think of my mother. I am of Hungarian and Austrian descent on my moms side and German on my dads side. Frikadellen was a staple in my home growing up. Pretty much the same recipe. Mom would buy a ground beef/veal/pork blend if available, otherwise just beef. Delicious either way. She did not add paprika. Please resist the temptation to make this into a meatloaf. It simply is not the same as a well-seared burger. Serve with homemade potato pancakes and whatever veggie you like.

Been making these for many many years. You can use regular sweet paprika if you do t want the heat. I also soak my stale crusty bread in milk instead of water. I need to go Make some more. They do well in the freezer or in the fridge, then take one, slice it in half width wise make a sandwich with mustard HMMMMMMM
My German grandmother would brown the patties then remove them from pan and make a gravy, usually onion, and then simmer the patties until they were cooked through. Love this meal!

I’m German and have been making theses since I could cook. Never used the hot paprika though. And if you don’t have a Kaiser roll a slice or two of white bread works fine. It’s what My mom always used. I put the dry bread in a mini chopper (with or without the crust - your choice) and then just add a splash of milk to my meat. They’re great leftover and can be eaten room temp. Great with German potato salad!!!

I have been making this recipe for over 40 years. My German sister in law taught me her family recipe when we lived in Germany. The only differences are she used oregano and after the patties were made she dredged them in bread crumbs and then pan fried them. We lived in the Lahr region so it could have been a regional difference. Regardless, they are now and have been a family favorite all these years. We always have them with homemade spaetzle and pan gravy. 🤤
This makes very moist burgers and I plan on making them again. The main thing I will change though is that I will do them on the grill
Anyone suggesting trying this as a meatloaf has not made the recipe. But to be true German Frikadellen, this recipe needs marjoram and nutmeg.

Just like Oma used to make it, forgot about it over the many years. Definitely will be making it tonight. Don't have a kaiser roll, so a thick slice of French bread will have to do, also she used a little grated garlic if I remember correctly. Brings back memories from 70 years ago. Thank you.
Delicious
Similar to my grandmother's recipe. Hers has 1/3 ground beef 1/3 ground pork 1/3 ground veal.

We love these! But my Oma and mother would brown them quickly and then finish cooking them in brown gravy and serve with mashed potatoes and a green vegetable. My boys are all grown and living on their own but will still ask for me to make for them.
Ukrainians call them kptlety...most Baltic countries have the same thing with names that sound close.
Basically it's just a Meatloaf turned into a Burger Patty, nothing special. Oma used to make them and called them Fleischkuechle. Badenser style.

My mother is Jewish with a Romanian heritage. We call these kekletin. Made with just beef because of Jewish dietary laws. We make the same way but roll in breadcrumbs before frying. A family favorite for over 60 years

For anyone saying these are bland, everyone has their own recipe in Germany and there is the spices to their taste. Also, the meat to bread ratio. You can use plain or seasoned bread crumbs as well. This is a fantastic base recipe for the intro of what a Frikadelle or Boulette (Berlin) is. I put a dash of send or German mustard in mine, really makes the recipe. Unlike some of the comments suggest, they are frequently eaten on rolls called Brötchen in Germany, with either ketchup or senf. They are also great cold for picnics.
Absolutely love it, i made it to night, juicy and full of flavour.
easy to make
